name: runpod-gpu-v3-fullres
description: runpod-gpu-v3.json with the client-side downscale OFF -- the full-resolution control that prices what image_max_long_edge 896 costs (or buys) on GPU. Identical in every other field, and it writes to its own out_dir so the two runs can never merge into one results.json. Run this one FIRST if the question is accuracy (the downscale is a recall risk, not a free win), or second if the question is latency. A separate config rather than a CLI flag because the harness has no --image-max-long-edge override and a run's resolution belongs in the artifact that describes the run.
_image_max_long_edge_note: null == send the corpus bytes as-is (mostly 1280 px long edge). Compare prompt_tokens against runpod-gpu-v3's to confirm the 896 run actually halved image tokens; ~(896/1280)^2 = 0.49x is the expectation.
_env_note: Same ${RUNPOD_QWEN_URL} contract as runpod-gpu-v3.json -- expanded by harness.runner.expand_env, unset is a hard error. Point BOTH runs at the same pod and the same loaded weights, or the resolution comparison is confounded.

runpod_qwen_vl._headers_note: Runpod's HTTP proxy (*.proxy.runpod.net) 403s any request whose User-Agent starts with 'Python-urllib' -- the harness's default, since providers.py posts via urllib. Verified 2026-08-12: identical POST bodies, UA 'Python-urllib/3.14' -> 403, 'openplate-eval/3' -> 200. Without this override every record in the run errors instantly with ProviderHttpError(403) (403 is not retried -- only 429/5xx are). Any non-urllib UA works; keep it honest rather than spoofing a browser.

single_qwen_vl_v3.label: v3 terse single-shot Qwen3-VL, remote Runpod GPU, full resolution

_run_notes: Do not run this back-to-back over the same images as the 896 run without accounting for the server's prompt-prefix cache: a warm cache flatters the second run's prefill (PERFORMANCE.md §6). Different image bytes means different prefix, so cross-run contamination is unlikely here, but a re-run of the SAME config is cache-warm.

If Pillow is missing on the client, runpod-gpu-v3.json degrades into this config while still labelling itself 896 px. The harness prints one WARN to stderr -- that warning is the only difference between a valid comparison and two identical runs.
